Answer:



The pie chart illustrates what Anthropology students of a certain university ended up doing after graduating, while the table outlines the average salaries these graduates earn 5 years after the start of their employment.



Overall, it can be observed that a great proportion of Anthropology graduates opted for full-time work, whereas the least proportion decided to pursue postgraduate studies along with part-time work. Additionally, the majority of the salaries of graduates with 5 years of experience fall under the category of 100 thousand dollars and above.



While just over a half of Anthropology graduates chose to get a full-time job, only 8% were interested in pursuing full-time further studies, which was matched by those with unknown careers. The figure for part-time workers was 15%. Similarly, those who tried to combine postgraduate studies and part-time work were a minority, at only 5%. Finally, just over a tenth of these graduates remained unemployed.



As for money earnings after 5 years of employment, half of the people working in the government sector earn 100,000 dollars or more, whereas, just under a third of the people in private companies make the same amount of money. Freelance workers, however, have pretty high earnings, where 40% of them earn between $75,000 – $99,999 and another 40% earn over this amount. A small proportion of workers earn between $25,000 – $49,999 in the three types of employment.
